lesson_1.topicLabel: Enquiry 01: Building the Round City of Baghdad (AD 750–900)
lesson_1.title: Why Was the Round City of Baghdad Built, and How Big Did It Grow?
lesson_1.spokenTitle: Why was the Round City of Baghdad built, and how big did it grow?

cards.heading: Choosing the River Tigris
cards.connective: Why was the Round City of Baghdad built, and how big did it grow?
cards.html: In AD 762, Abbasid Caliph al-Mansur chose a fertile bend on the River Tigris for his new capital. Deep canals watered green crops and linked round river boats to Silk Road routes.
cards.spoken: Why was the Round City of Baghdad built, and how big did it grow? <short pause> In AD 762 , Abbasid Caliph al-Mansur chose a fertile bend on the River Tigris for his new capital. Deep canals watered green crops and linked round river boats to Silk Road routes.

cards.heading: The Round City of Peace
cards.stat: 2km Brick Circle, 4 Iron Gates & Green Dome
cards.connective: Next, al-Mansur gathered 100,000 workers to build a remarkable circular capital.
cards.html: Traced in flaming cotton seeds, Baghdad's Round City rose inside double mud-brick walls called Madinat al-Salam. Four iron gates led straight to the Great Mosque and Palace.
cards.spoken: Next, al-Mansur gathered 100,000 workers to build a remarkable circular capital. <short pause> Traced in flaming cotton seeds, Baghdad's Round City rose inside double mud-brick walls called Madinat al-Salam . Four iron gates led straight to the Great Mosque and Palace .

cards.heading: Baghdad vs Anglo-Saxon Towns
cards.connective: Markets and gardens soon spilled far beyond the original circular walls.
cards.html: By AD 900, paved streets, canals, and libraries served nearly one million people in Baghdad. Meanwhile, smoky timber towns in Anglo-Saxon Britain held only 5,000 to 10,000 residents.
cards.spoken: Markets and gardens soon spilled far beyond the original circular walls. <short pause> By AD 900 , paved streets, canals, and libraries served nearly one million people in Baghdad. Meanwhile, smoky timber towns in Anglo-Saxon Britain held only 5,000 to 10,000 residents.

cards.heading: Crossroads of Three Continents
cards.stat: One of Earth's Largest & Richest Cities
cards.connective: Clever planning and river waterways turned Baghdad into a world capital.
cards.html: Linked by river canals and desert trails, the City of Peace outgrew tiny European towns. Its bustling gates welcomed traders, craftworkers, and scholars from three continents.
cards.spoken: Clever planning and river waterways turned Baghdad into a world capital. <short pause> Linked by river canals and desert trails, the City of Peace outgrew tiny European towns. Its bustling gates welcomed traders, craftworkers, and scholars from three continents.

lesson_1.takeaway: Founded by Caliph al-Mansur beside the River Tigris in AD 762, circular Baghdad grew to nearly one million people—dwarfing Anglo-Saxon towns in Britain.
vocab: 1. Caliph
Supreme political and spiritual ruler of the early Islamic Empire.
2. Canals
Human-made waterways dug to water crops and carry trading boats.
3. Madinat al-Salam
Arabic for 'City of Peace', official name of Round Baghdad.
lesson_1.provenanceNote: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Bibliothèque nationale de France, British Museum, Khalili Collections & Wikimedia Commons (Zero AI Imagery)
lesson_1.spokenTakeaway: Here is the big story in one sentence. <short pause> Founded by Caliph al-Mansur beside the River Tigris in AD 762, circular Baghdad grew to nearly one million people, dwarfing Anglo-Saxon towns in Britain.

lesson_2.topicLabel: Enquiry 02: Paper & The House of Wisdom (c. AD 800–1000)
lesson_2.title: How Did Cheap Paper and Baghdad's House of Wisdom Save World Knowledge?
lesson_2.spokenTitle: How did cheap paper and Baghdad's House of Wisdom save world knowledge?

cards.heading: Rag Paper & 100+ Bookshops
cards.stat: Samarkand Paper Mills vs Costly Calfskin
cards.connective: How did cheap paper and Baghdad's House of Wisdom save world knowledge?
cards.html: Caliphs Harun al-Rashid and al-Ma'mun expanded Baghdad's royal House of Wisdom. Using Chinese rag paper-making from Samarkand, over 100 bookshops buzzed while Europe scraped costly parchment.
cards.spoken: How did cheap paper and Baghdad's House of Wisdom save world knowledge? <short pause> Caliphs Harun al-Rashid and al-Ma'mun expanded Baghdad's royal House of Wisdom . Using Chinese rag paper-making from Samarkand, over 100 bookshops buzzed while Europe scraped costly parchment.

cards.heading: Translating Ancient Scrolls
cards.stat: Greek, Persian & Sanskrit Texts into Arabic
cards.connective: Inside the academy, scholars of different faiths worked side by side.
cards.html: Muslim, Christian, and Jewish thinkers led the Translation Movement into Arabic. Star doctor Hunayn ibn Ishaq translated medical scrolls while scholars tested old claims and fixed mistakes.
cards.spoken: Inside the academy, scholars of different faiths worked side by side. <short pause> Muslim, Christian, and Jewish thinkers led the Translation Movement into Arabic . Star doctor Hunayn ibn Ishaq translated medical scrolls while scholars tested old claims and fixed mistakes.

cards.heading: Fatima al-Fihri & Zubayda
cards.stat: AD 859 Fez College & Desert Hajj Wells
cards.connective: Generous women patrons also funded lasting colleges and desert lifelines.
cards.html: In AD 859, Fatima al-Fihri founded al-Qarawiyyin college in Fez, where students still study today. Earlier, Baghdad's Queen Zubayda funded stone wells along the hot Hajj road.
cards.spoken: Generous women patrons also funded lasting colleges and desert lifelines. <short pause> In AD 859, Fatima al-Fihri founded al-Qarawiyyin college in Fez, where students still study today. Earlier, Baghdad's Queen Zubayda funded stone wells along the hot Hajj road.

cards.heading: World Knowledge Saved & Tested
cards.connective: Together, cheap paper, translators, and patrons sparked a Golden Age.
cards.html: Instead of letting fragile scrolls crumble, Baghdad's paper mills and House of Wisdom rescued ancient learning. Testing every idea carefully launched bold new science.
cards.spoken: Together, cheap paper, translators, and patrons sparked a Golden Age. <short pause> Instead of letting fragile scrolls crumble, Baghdad's paper mills and House of Wisdom rescued ancient learning. Testing every idea carefully launched bold new science .

lesson_2.takeaway: Cheap rag paper, Baghdad's House of Wisdom translators, and patrons like Fatima al-Fihri rescued ancient scrolls and sparked fresh Golden Age discoveries.
vocab: 1. House of Wisdom
Baghdad's famous royal library and research academy (Bayt al-Hikma).
2. Translation Movement
Effort turning Greek, Persian, and Indian scrolls into Arabic.
3. Patrons
Wealthy supporters who funded libraries, colleges, or public wells.
lesson_2.provenanceNote: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Bibliothèque nationale de France, British Museum, Khalili Collections & Wikimedia Commons (Zero AI Imagery)
lesson_2.spokenTakeaway: Here is the big story in one sentence. <short pause> Cheap rag paper, Baghdad's House of Wisdom translators, and patrons like Fatima al-Fihri rescued ancient scrolls and sparked fresh Golden Age discoveries.

lesson_3.topicLabel: Enquiry 03: Zero, Astrolabes & Free Hospitals (c. AD 820–1050)
lesson_3.title: What Amazing Discoveries Did Baghdad's Doctors and Scientists Make?
lesson_3.spokenTitle: What amazing discoveries did Baghdad's doctors and scientists make?

cards.heading: Zero, Algebra & Star Tools
cards.connective: What amazing discoveries did Baghdad's doctors and scientists make?
cards.html: Al-Khwarizmi championed digits 0 to 9 and wrote the book that gave us algebra. Meanwhile, Mariam al-Asturlabi crafted brass astrolabes and al-Jazari built his Elephant Clock.
cards.spoken: What amazing discoveries did Baghdad's doctors and scientists make? <short pause> Al-Khwarizmi championed digits 0 to 9 and wrote the book that gave us algebra . Meanwhile, Mariam al-Asturlabi crafted brass astrolabes and al-Jazari built his Elephant Clock.

cards.heading: Light Tests & Free Hospitals
cards.stat: Pinhole Camera Obscura & Free Clean Wards
cards.connective: Scientists also tested how human eyes see and opened hospitals for all.
cards.html: Using a dark pinhole camera obscura, Ibn al-Haytham proved light travels straight into our eyes. Cities also built free bimaristan hospitals with clean wards and pharmacies.
cards.spoken: Scientists also tested how human eyes see and opened hospitals for all. <short pause> Using a dark pinhole camera obscura , Ibn al-Haytham proved light travels straight into our eyes. Cities also built free bimaristan hospitals with clean wards and pharmacies.

cards.heading: Doctors Al-Razi & Al-Zahrawi
cards.connective: Careful bedside notes and clever new tools helped sick patients heal.
cards.html: Chief doctor al-Razi picked Baghdad's cleanest air and told measles apart from smallpox. In Spain, surgeon al-Zahrawi drew 200 surgical tools and discovered dissolving catgut stitches.
cards.spoken: Careful bedside notes and clever new tools helped sick patients heal. <short pause> Chief doctor al-Razi picked Baghdad's cleanest air and told measles apart from smallpox. In Spain, surgeon al-Zahrawi drew 200 surgical tools and discovered dissolving catgut stitches.

cards.heading: Foundations of Modern Science
cards.connective: Testing ideas through real experiments transformed maths, optics, and medicine.
cards.html: From algorithms and zero to pinhole optics and free hospital wards, Islamic scholars checked evidence rather than guessing. Their breakthroughs power modern computers and medicine.
cards.spoken: Testing ideas through real experiments transformed maths, optics, and medicine. <short pause> From algorithms and zero to pinhole optics and free hospital wards , Islamic scholars checked evidence rather than guessing. Their breakthroughs power modern computers and medicine .

lesson_3.takeaway: Scholars like al-Khwarizmi, Ibn al-Haytham, al-Razi, and al-Zahrawi transformed world science with zero, algebra, pinhole optics, surgical tools, and free hospitals.
vocab: 1. Algebra
Maths using balanced equations, named after al-Khwarizmi's al-Jabr.
2. Astrolabe
Engraved brass star tool for telling time and sailing oceans.
3. Bimaristan
Free Islamic teaching hospital with clean wards and a pharmacy.
lesson_3.provenanceNote: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Bibliothèque nationale de France, British Museum, Khalili Collections & Wikimedia Commons (Zero AI Imagery)

lesson_4.topicLabel: Enquiry 04: Silk Road Caravans, Dhows & Viking Coins (c. AD 850–1000)
lesson_4.title: How Did Baghdad's Traders Connect the World All the Way to Britain?
lesson_4.spokenTitle: How did Baghdad's traders connect the world all the way to Britain?

cards.heading: Bazaars & Silk Road Caravans
cards.connective: How did Baghdad's traders connect the world all the way to Britain?
cards.html: Shaded bazaars gleamed with Chinese silk, Indian spices, and blown glass carried by camel caravans. Every thirty kilometres, walled caravanserai inns sheltered traders safely along the Silk Road.
cards.spoken: How did Baghdad's traders connect the world all the way to Britain? <short pause> Shaded bazaars gleamed with Chinese silk, Indian spices, and blown glass carried by camel caravans. Every thirty kilometres, walled caravanserai inns sheltered traders safely along the Silk Road .

cards.heading: Ocean Dhows & Paper Cheques
cards.stat: Stitched Wooden Hulls & Signed Sakk Notes
cards.connective: South from Basra port, sailors also rode ocean winds towards India and China.
cards.html: Captains steered stitched wooden dhow ships across the Indian Ocean using brass astrolabes. Instead of hauling heavy coin sacks, merchants cashed signed paper sakk cheques afar.
cards.spoken: South from Basra port, sailors also rode ocean winds towards India and China. <short pause> Captains steered stitched wooden dhow ships across the Indian Ocean using brass astrolabes . Instead of hauling heavy coin sacks, merchants cashed signed paper sakk cheques afar.

cards.heading: Silver Dirhams in Viking York
cards.stat: Jorvik Silver Hoards & King Offa's Gold Coin
cards.connective: Archaeologists have even dug up Baghdad's coins in Scandinavian and British soil.
cards.html: Pure silver dirhams travelled up Russian rivers to Vikings, who buried hoards near Jorvik (York). Earlier, Mercia's King Offa even minted a gold coin copying Arabic script.
cards.spoken: Archaeologists have even dug up Baghdad's coins in Scandinavian and British soil. <short pause> Pure silver dirhams travelled up Russian rivers to Vikings, who buried hoards near Jorvik (York) . Earlier, Mercia's King Offa even minted a gold coin copying Arabic script.

cards.heading: From China Right to Britain
cards.stat: Three Continents Linked by Ships & Caravans
cards.connective: Overland trails, ocean sails, and river routes wove a giant trading web.
cards.html: Baghdad's caravans, dhow ships, and trusted silver dirhams linked Asia, Africa, and Europe. Goods, banking ideas, and coins reached all the way to medieval Britain.
cards.spoken: Overland trails, ocean sails, and river routes wove a giant trading web. <short pause> Baghdad's caravans, dhow ships , and trusted silver dirhams linked Asia, Africa, and Europe. Goods, banking ideas, and coins reached all the way to medieval Britain .

lesson_4.takeaway: Camel caravans, stitched Indian Ocean dhows, paper sakk cheques, and trusted silver dirhams connected Baghdad's markets from China all the way to Viking Britain.
vocab: 1. Caravanserai
Walled roadside inn built every 30 km for Silk Road caravans.
2. Sakk
Signed paper payment slip cashed afar—origin of our word cheque.
3. Dirham
Pure silver coin with Arabic script found in Viking York hoards.
lesson_4.provenanceNote: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Bibliothèque nationale de France, British Museum, Khalili Collections & Wikimedia Commons (Zero AI Imagery)
lesson_4.spokenTakeaway: Here is the big story in one sentence. <short pause> Camel caravans, stitched Indian Ocean dhows, paper sakk cheques, and trusted silver dirhams connected Baghdad's markets from China all the way to Viking Britain.

lesson_5.topicLabel: Enquiry 05: Courtyards, Tilework & Chess in Baghdad (c. AD 900)
lesson_5.title: What Was Everyday Family Life Like in Baghdad Around AD 900?
lesson_5.spokenTitle: What was everyday family life like in Baghdad around AD 900?

cards.heading: Windcatchers & Clean Hammams
cards.connective: What was everyday family life like in Baghdad around AD 900?
cards.html: Rooftop windcatcher towers scooped breezes into shaded fountain courtyards during hot summers. Neighbours also washed with olive-oil soap and sweet rosewater inside tiled public hammams.
cards.spoken: What was everyday family life like in Baghdad around AD 900? <short pause> Rooftop windcatcher towers scooped breezes into shaded fountain courtyards during hot summers. Neighbours also washed with olive-oil soap and sweet rosewater inside tiled public hammams .

cards.heading: Citrus Feasts & Star Tilework
cards.connective: Waterwheels fed lush orchards while master tilers decorated calm mosque walls.
cards.html: Families enjoyed lemons, oranges, and cane sugar served on shiny lustreware bowls. Avoiding statues in mosques, artists crafted geometric stars, leafy arabesques, and flowing Arabic calligraphy.
cards.spoken: Waterwheels fed lush orchards while master tilers decorated calm mosque walls. <short pause> Families enjoyed lemons, oranges, and cane sugar served on shiny lustreware bowls. Avoiding statues in mosques, artists crafted geometric stars , leafy arabesques, and flowing Arabic calligraphy .

cards.heading: Glass Lamps & Shatranj Chess
cards.stat: Silk Tiraz Robes, Gilded Glass & Checkmate
cards.connective: As evening breezes cooled the courtyard, families gathered on woven carpets.
cards.html: Workshops wove silk tiraz robes and gilded glowing glass mosque lamps. At dusk, families sipped fruit syrups and played shatranj chess, shouting Shah mat — our word checkmate!
cards.spoken: As evening breezes cooled the courtyard, families gathered on woven carpets. <short pause> Workshops wove silk tiraz robes and gilded glowing glass mosque lamps . At dusk, families sipped fruit syrups and played shatranj chess , shouting Shah mat, our word checkmate!

cards.heading: Comfort, Beauty & Clever Craft
cards.connective: Science, trade, and skilled craft made daily life comfortable and vibrant.
cards.html: From breezy courtyard homes and steamed hammams to star mosaics and chess, Baghdad blended beauty with clever design. Many foods and games reached homes worldwide.
cards.spoken: Science, trade, and skilled craft made daily life comfortable and vibrant. <short pause> From breezy courtyard homes and steamed hammams to star mosaics and chess , Baghdad blended beauty with clever design. Many foods and games reached homes worldwide .

lesson_5.takeaway: Around AD 900, Baghdad families enjoyed windcatcher-cooled courtyards, clean hammam bathhouses, citrus foods, geometric star tilework, and shatranj chess.
vocab: 1. Windcatcher
Rooftop cooling tower funnelling fresh breezes down indoors.
2. Hammam
Steamed public bathhouse where neighbours washed with soap.
3. Calligraphy
Artistic Arabic handwriting turning sacred verses into visual art.

lesson_6.topicLabel: Enquiry 06: The 1258 Siege of Baghdad & Surviving Ideas
lesson_6.title: Why Did Baghdad Fall in 1258, and How Did Its Ideas Survive?
lesson_6.spokenTitle: Why did Baghdad fall in 1258, and how did its ideas survive?

cards.heading: AD 1258: Mongol Siege & Fall
cards.stat: Hulagu Khan's Trebuchets Break Brick Walls
cards.connective: Why did Baghdad fall in 1258, and how did its ideas survive?
cards.html: In January 1258, Hulagu Khan's Mongol army surrounded weakened Baghdad and fired giant wooden trebuchets. Fires ruined canals and the House of Wisdom, ending Abbasid rule.
cards.spoken: Why did Baghdad fall in 1258, and how did its ideas survive? <short pause> In January 1258 , Hulagu Khan's Mongol army surrounded weakened Baghdad and fired giant wooden trebuchets . Fires ruined canals and the House of Wisdom, ending Abbasid rule.

cards.heading: Saved in Cairo, Córdoba & Toledo
cards.connective: Even when Baghdad's library burned, Golden Age books were not lost.
cards.html: Paper copies survived safely in Cairo, Samarkand, and Córdoba in Islamic Al-Andalus. In Spanish Toledo, Muslim, Jewish, and Christian translators turned Arabic science into Latin.
cards.spoken: Even when Baghdad's library burned, Golden Age books were not lost. <short pause> Paper copies survived safely in Cairo, Samarkand, and Córdoba in Islamic Al-Andalus . In Spanish Toledo , Muslim, Jewish, and Christian translators turned Arabic science into Latin.

cards.heading: Arabic Words & Maths Today
cards.connective: Those rescued books helped spark Europe's Renaissance and shape our world today.
cards.html: Every sum using digits 0 to 9, phone algorithm, and camera lens builds on Golden Age science. Everyday English words like zero, sugar, lemon, and sofa come from Arabic.
cards.spoken: Those rescued books helped spark Europe's Renaissance and shape our world today. <short pause> Every sum using digits 0 to 9 , phone algorithm , and camera lens builds on Golden Age science. Everyday English words like zero, sugar, lemon, and sofa come from Arabic.

cards.heading: Walls Fell, Wisdom Lived On
cards.connective: Copying books onto paper meant no single siege could erase human learning.
cards.html: Although Mongol trebuchets broke Baghdad's walls in 1258, libraries from Cairo to Spain kept its discoveries safe. Early Islamic science and words still enrich daily life.
cards.spoken: Copying books onto paper meant no single siege could erase human learning. <short pause> Although Mongol trebuchets broke Baghdad's walls in 1258, libraries from Cairo to Spain kept its discoveries safe. Early Islamic science and words still enrich daily life.

lesson_6.takeaway: Hulagu Khan's Mongol siege destroyed Baghdad in 1258, yet paper copies in Cairo, Córdoba, and Toledo saved Islamic maths, medicine, and words for today.
vocab: 1. Trebuchet
Giant counterweight catapult used to hurl boulders at walls.
2. Al-Andalus
Medieval Islamic Spain and Portugal, famed for great libraries.
3. Renaissance
Europe's rebirth of science and art, aided by Arabic books.
